content:
Emily Zhao: hey runtime folks — for hot-route protection we need a backpressure signal we can use in router admission. what’s actually reliable? we’ve been staring at GPU util but it’s kinda all over the place

Vikram Singh: +1. router wants something we can sample frequently and trust. queue depth? in-flight tokens? looking for guidance before we wire anything up

Mina Haddad: specifically: want a signal that correlates with “tail latency about to go bad” so we can start shedding low tier. GPU util has false positives (prefill spikes) and also stays low sometimes when we’re actually backed up

Sofia Ivanova: yup GPU util is not a great “is this shard overloaded” signal. it’s noisy (kernel scheduling, prefill bursts, cuda graphs, etc) and tends to lag the thing you care about

Sofia Ivanova: the most reliable leading indicator for *latency pain* is queueing inside the scheduler

Julian Moore: +1. if you want one metric to drive admission: `decode_queue_depth` (or queue time) beats GPU util every time

Lena Fischer: breakdown from runtime side:
- **Queue depth / queue time** (per-engine): reliable, fast to compute, strongly correlated w p99
- **Active sequences / in-flight reqs**: decent, but depends on sequence length distribution
- **GPU util**: good for capacity planning / dashboards; bad for gating (too jittery, not request-path actionable)
- **tokens/sec**: good trend metric but you need windowing + it lags; can be misleading during throttling
- **KV cache hit/evict**: good for “why is it expensive”, not “should i shed now”

Emily Zhao: when you say queue depth, where exactly? router sees a pool of engines behind a shard; we can ingest per-node signals but cardinality gets scary

Julian Moore: the internal scheduler has two relevant queues:
- prefill admission queue (short bursts)
- decode queue (the one that kills p99)

Julian Moore: if you only expose one, expose decode queue depth and/or `queue_wait_ms` histogram (p95 over last N secs)

Vikram Singh: would `queue_wait_ms_p95_5s` work? we can sample and feed into policy engine

Sofia Ivanova: careful w histos in the loop. recommend a simple gauge for admission:
- `decode_queue_depth` (gauge)
- optionally `oldest_decode_queue_age_ms`

Sofia Ivanova: and set thresholds conservatively. queue depth has less jitter than util

Mina Haddad: what about GPU memory pressure? we’ve seen cases where util is low but we’re thrashing / OOM-ing

Lena Fischer: memory pressure is real but it’s usually “already broken” not “approaching broken”. as a trigger it’s too late (you’ll be in retries / 5xx land)

Lena Fischer: that said, a “circuit breaker” signal like `oom_recent=true` or `kv_evictions_rate_high` can be used for failover/fallback routing, not for normal shedding

Sean Gallagher: from SRE angle: we need a signal that’s stable enough to alert on too. GPU util alerts = pager spam. queue age seems more aligned w incidents

Allison Grant: +1 on cardinality. please don’t ship per-model-per-route-per-engine metrics into the central TSDB. can we keep this aggregated at “pool/shard + tier lane”?

Caleb Johnson: if you’re emitting from runtime -> mesh -> router, can you also annotate w a small set of labels? region, pool_id, engine_role maybe. anything else will be expensive

Emily Zhao: ok so proposal: runtime emits (per pool) `decode_queue_depth` and `oldest_decode_queue_age_ms` and router aggregates/uses that for admission. sampling frequency?

Julian Moore: sampling freq guidance:
- don’t do sub-second polling from router. it’s too chatty and you’ll chase noise
- 2s is usually fine
- 5s is safer for overhead but may react slower to retry storms

Sofia Ivanova: we can push updates every 2s without hurting the runtime, but only if it’s a cheap gauge read. anything that requires scanning queues / recomputing histos every time will hurt

Sofia Ivanova: also: if you sample too often, policy will oscillate (shed, recover, shed). add hysteresis on the router side

Mina Haddad: +1. we can add a “cooldown” window (e.g., once we start shedding, keep it on for 15-30s) and only disable when below threshold for X seconds

Vikram Singh: do we have recommended thresholds? like decode_queue_depth > N? depends on model size / batch

Lena Fischer: thresholds are model+hardware dependent, yeah. but you can pick a proxy:
- normalize by `max_concurrent_decode` (engine config)
- or just use `oldest_decode_queue_age_ms` since that’s closer to SLO

Lena Fischer: if oldest decode queue age > 250ms for >10s, you’re basically going to start missing p99 soon (for chat). for long-form, tune higher

Sean Gallagher: +0 on queue age. lets tie it to the enterprise SLOs (p99). easier to explain in postmortems than “gpu util was 83%”

Allison Grant: +1 explainability matters for the dashboards too

Emily Zhao: can you confirm GPU util is still ok for “fleet saturation” pages but not for admission? i want to document this in the design

Sofia Ivanova: yes. GPU util for capacity planning + “are we burning money idle” + general health dashboards. for admission control, prefer queueing signals

Caleb Johnson: small note: if router uses queue age, make sure it’s monotonic-ish. clocks across nodes can skew. maybe compute age locally in runtime using monotonic clock and ship the age as a value

Julian Moore: good catch. we already have monotonic timers in the scheduler, can export `oldest_decode_queue_age_ms` computed locally

Mina Haddad: what about `prefill_saturation`? we have bursty prefill that can tank first-token lat

Lena Fischer: prefill saturation is real, but it’s spiky and usually short-lived. if you gate on it you’ll over-throttle. better: separate signal for “first token latency at risk” if you want, but for hot-route protection the big issue is sustained decode backlog

Sean Gallagher: can we do both but w different actions? e.g., prefill spike -> reduce batching or shed free tier; decode backlog -> strict enterprise lane

Sofia Ivanova: yeah, but keep v1 simple: decode queue age triggers tier shedding. add prefill later once we have stable instrumentation

Emily Zhao: ok. action items:
1) runtime to provide `decode_queue_depth` + `oldest_decode_queue_age_ms` per pool (2s publish)
2) router to add hysteresis + cooldown
3) avoid GPU util in admission loop, keep for dashboards

Vikram Singh: works for me. we’ll wire in the gauges and put the rest behind a feature flag

Julian Moore: i’ll drop the metric names + units in a short doc and share in #eng-platform

Sofia Ivanova: ack. ping me if you need help interpreting spikes during load test

Allison Grant: please route the metric naming through observability standards before it lands (:eyes:)

Emily Zhao: will do. thanks all :thumbsup:

(Sean Gallagher reacted with :thumbsup:)
(Allison Grant reacted with :white_check_mark:)
